entities.name: death of Osama bin Laden
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The death of Osama bin Laden was a pivotal moment in the War on Terror, signaling a significant blow to al-Qaeda's leadership and operations. 

On May 2, 2011, a U.S. military operation in Abbottabad, Pakistan, resulted in the taking out of Osama bin Laden, the mastermind behind the September 11 attacks in 2001. 

This event marked a crucial turning point in the conflict, with the U.S. and its allies pushing to dismantle al-Qaeda's network and disrupt its ability to plan and execute future attacks. 

The legacy of the death of Osama bin Laden can be seen in the increased global cooperation to combat terrorism and the subsequent decline in al-Qaeda's influence.

As a senior al-Qaeda leader once said, 52,000 worth of damages was incurred in a single operation.6
